title: Palay Price Today in the Philippines: Per Kilo, Per Cavan and NFA Rates
metaTitle: Palay Price Today: Per Kilo, Per Cavan and NFA Rates
metaDescription: Palay price today: the latest PSA farmgate price per kilo, the NFA buying price for wet and dry palay, the price per cavan, and how moisture sets it.
excerpt: The palay price you get depends on the month, your province, the variety and how dry your grain is. Here is the latest PSA farmgate average and the NFA buying price. You will also see what those mean per cavan, and how to check a buyer's offer before you sell.

heroImage.alt: A farmer checking his notebook beside tall stacks of sacks in a farm shed

blocks.text: Prices move every week, so treat the numbers below as a snapshot taken on 30 September 2026. Each one links to its source in the list at the end, and you can check them again before you haul.
A cavan, rice farmers' usual unit, holds about 50 kilos of palay. The rice palay price, Philippines wide, is reported each week by the PSA as the farmgate price per kilo.
Palay price today: the latest PSA farmgate average

The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) tracks the farmgate price of dry palay every month. For August 2026, the latest month out when we wrote this, the national average was P22.16 per kilogram. That was 29.9 percent higher than in August 2025, but 1 percent lower than in July 2026. In June 2026 the average stood at P21.78.

The gap between places was wide. Central Visayas averaged P28.07 per kilo, while the Bangsamoro region stood at P20.61. Cavite posted the biggest monthly drop of any province, down 16.4 percent to P17.16, though that is still 47.9 percent above a year earlier.

blocks.caption: Farmgate price of dry palay per kilo, August 2026 (PSA data as reported by BusinessWorld)

blocks.text: Palay price per kilo today from the NFA

The National Food Authority (NFA) buys palay straight from farmers at set prices. On 28 September 2026, NFA Administrator Larry Lacson gave the rates for the wet season harvest. The agency will pay P22 per kilo for wet palay and P27 per kilo for dry palay. That harvest usually runs from September to November.

Before that, in July 2026, the DA ordered a minimum NFA buying price of P21 per kilo for wet palay, up from P17. The NFA is also moving to a purchase order system, which sets sales agreements with farmers before harvest. So ask your nearest NFA office about both the rate and the schedule before you haul.
Palay price per cavan
A cavan of palay weighs about 50 kg, so the price per cavan is the price per kilo times 50. Still, in Nueva Ecija PCIJ found sacks of 50 to 60 kg, so weigh before you agree on a sack price.

blocks.caption: Price per kilo and per 50 kg cavan
rows: PSA national average, dry palay, August 2026

blocks.text: Don't mix up the two cavans, either. A cavan of milled rice also weighs 50 kg. But at the PSA milling rate of 63 percent, it takes about 79 kg of palay to fill it.
How moisture, variety and grade set your palay price
Moisture: wet versus dry palay

According to PalayCheck, fresh grain from the harvester carries 18 to 21 percent moisture in the dry season. In the wet season it carries 20 to 25 percent. Buyers aim for about 14 percent. So when you dry, only water leaves the sack.

For example, 100 kg of palay at 24 percent moisture holds 76 kg of dry matter. Dried to 14 percent, it weighs about 88 kg. At the NFA rates, that is P2,200 sold wet or about P2,386 sold dry, before your drying cost. So compare every offer on the same moisture basis.
Variety, purity and the buyer

Variety counts too. In Nueva Ecija, PSA data for 2024 averaged P24.69 per kilo for dry fancy palay and P23.33 for other dry palay, PCIJ reported. So see our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) before you pick seed.

Clean grain sells better as well. PalayCheck advises removing chaff, straw and empty grains, because they hold moisture and cause hot spots in the sack. If a buyer is far away, a palay picture of a clean handful, taken in daylight, helps him judge your grain before he quotes. Finally, PCIJ found that agents in Nueva Ecija often add about 20 centavos per kilo to outbid each other. That is why it pays to ask more than one buyer.

blocks.title: Know your break even price
blocks.text: Divide your total season cost by your harvest in kilos. That gives the lowest palay price that still pays. If an offer falls below it, drying and storing may earn more than selling now.
From palay to rice: why rice costs more

Palay to rice conversion explains the gap between the two prices. At the PSA milling recovery rate of 63 percent, one kilo of milled rice needs about 1.59 kg of palay. At the August 2026 average of P22.16, that palay alone costs about P35 per kilo of rice. Drying, hauling, milling, packing and store margins come on top.

Some palay ends up in packed rice brands in the Philippines. Jasponica rice, for instance, is a premium rice that SL Agritech Corporation sells under its Doña Maria brand. So when you follow the rice and palay price in the Philippines, remember they track different products at different steps.
Why palay prices rise and fall

Prices usually dip at peak harvest, when everyone sells at once. Imports matter as well. For example, imports surged after the 2019 Rice Tariffication Law. Farmgate prices then fell sharply at the harvest peak of late 2019.

In 2026 the trend ran the other way, with monthly averages close to 30 percent above 2025. So plan your sale, not just your harvest. Our [palay guide](/crops/palay) shows how proper drying keeps your grain sound while you wait. Also, our [pagtatanim ng palay guide](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-palay) covers the harvest timing that protects milling quality.

blocks.text: Palay price questions farmers ask

items.q: What is the palay price today per kilo?
items.a: The latest PSA national average for dry palay was P22.16 per kilo in August 2026. Your local price can be several pesos higher or lower, so check the PSA farmgate page and ask more than one buyer.

items.q: How much is one cavan of palay?
items.a: Multiply the price per kilo by 50. At the August 2026 average of P22.16, a 50 kg cavan comes to about P1,108.

items.q: What is the NFA buying price of palay?
items.a: On 28 September 2026 the NFA said it will pay P22 per kilo for wet palay and P27 per kilo for dry palay during the wet season harvest. Confirm the rate with your nearest NFA office.
Part of its weight is water that dries off. For example, palay at 24 percent moisture loses about 12 percent of its weight when you dry it to 14 percent.

items.q: How many kilos of palay make one kilo of rice?
items.a: About 1.59 kg at the PSA milling recovery rate of 63 percent. Your mill and your grain quality can change that.
